governingStatute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (Act No. 12 of 2017)
title: Apportionment of credit and blocked input tax credits
plainTextSummary: Input Tax Credit (ITC) shall NOT be available in respect of statutory blocked credits under Section 17(5) of the CGST Act, 2017: (a) Motor vehicles for transportation of persons having approved seating capacity up to 13 persons (including driver), vessels, and aircraft, with narrow exceptions; (b)(i) Food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, cosmetic and plastic surgery, leasing/renting/hiring of motor vehicles; (b)(ii) Membership of a club, health and fitness centre; (b)(iii) Travel benefits extended to employees on vacation (LTC/home travel); (c) & (d) Works contract services and goods/services for construction of immovable property on own account; (h) Goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, or disposed of by way of gift or free samples (blocked regardless of value). Statutory Proviso Exception: ITC is permissible where: (1) inward supply is used for making outward taxable supply of the same category; or (2) where an employer is obligated by statutory law in force to provide the goods/services to employees (e.g. Factories Act, 1948 Section 46 mandatory canteen for factories with > 250 workers). Legal Note on Gifts: Under Section 17(5)(h), ITC on gifts is blocked irrespective of value. The ₹50,000 threshold in CGST Schedule I Entry 2 proviso relates solely to whether gifts by an employer to an employee constitute a deemed taxable supply without consideration, and does not permit ITC under Section 17(5).

keyStatutoryThresholds.giftTreatmentDistinction: Section 17(5)(h) blocks ITC on gifts and free samples regardless of value. The ₹50,000 threshold in CGST Schedule I Entry 2 proviso applies strictly to deemed supply valuation for employer-employee gifts, not to ITC eligibility.
keyStatutoryThresholds.erpImplementationGuidance: In standard corporate ERP systems (e.g. SAP/NetSuite), blocked input tax must not be credited to the Electronic Credit Ledger / Asset Account (e.g. standard COA Account 1400); it must be capitalized into the asset cost or expensed to the respective operating expense ledger (e.g. standard COA Account 5010). Account numbers 1400/5010 represent configurable ERP conventions, not statutory account codes.
